title: Opportunistic prompt micro-cache with occupancy-aware GPU reclamation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Prototype and roll out a lightweight per-request micro-cache for prompt prefixes that stores compact KV deltas and a semantic fingerprint. Introduce an occupancy-aware GPU reclaimer that opportunistically compacts or evicts micro-cache entries when per-GPU resident memory falls below configurable thresholds. Goal: increase cross-request prompt reuse while minimizing steady-state GPU memory pressure and avoiding tail-latency regressions.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end POC integrated with runtime that can return a cache hit for identical or near-identical prompt prefixes
Measured 90th and 95th percentile latency impact <= +5ms relative to baseline for warm-paths
Sustained GPU resident memory reduction of at least 10% on representative multi-tenant load during steady-state
Feature flag to disable micro-cache per-cluster and per-model, with safe fallback to existing KV restore path
Canary rollout plan and dashboards for hit-rate, memory churn, and correctness regressions
decisions: Use a two-layer cache: L1 in-host microcache (CPU) with semantic fingerprints, L2 as compact GPU-resident KV slices for hot entries
Fingerprinting will use lightweight SimHash over tokenized prompts plus normalized prompt template ID to allow tolerant matching rather than exact string hashes
Eviction policy: tenant-weighted LRU augmented with reference counts derived from active batch affinity to avoid evicting in-flight shared slices
GPU reclamation will be occupancy-aware: only trigger async compaction when resident GPU memory falls below low-watermark and background compaction budget is available
tradeoffs: Semantic fingerprints increase false positives risk - mitigated by a checksum validation step before applying cached KV deltas
Maintaining L1 micro-cache uses host memory and adds CPU cycles to check fingerprints for each request; must ensure CPU overhead < 1% of request CPU budget
Aggressive compaction reduces memory but increases background GPU cycles and may reduce available HBM for active batches temporarily
tasks: Design review: formalize micro-cache entry schema and serialized compact delta format (Maya)
Implement L1 fingerprint index and probe path in request router (Arjun)
Add GPU slice allocation metadata and reference counting hooks to KV manager (Samir)
Build async compactor that can merge small KV deltas into contiguous GPU slices (engine infra)
Unit/integration tests for checksum validation and rollback on mismatch (QA)
Bench harness: replay production traces with varying sequence-length distributions (Perf)
Dashboard: hit-rate, miss cost (ms), memory churn, compaction cycles, and 95th latency delta (Observability)
Security review and KMS consideration for any logged prompt-derived fingerprints (Security)
Prepare canary plan and featureflag rollout (SRE)
Documentation: runtime config knobs and operational runbook (Docs)
Attach PR and design doc links when available
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint collisions: synthetic inputs producing near-identical fingerprints should be validated and rejected when checksums mismatch
Simulated multi-tenant replay showing memory savings and hit-rate distribution by tenant across 24h traces
Latency regression tests with cold/warm paths capturing 50/90/95/99th percentiles
Fault injection: intentionally return corrupted micro-cache payloads to verify safe rollback to full KV restore
Canary A/B on 10% traffic for 72h with auto-rollback thresholds for correctness, p95 latency, and memory increase
notes: Avoid coupling micro-cache keys to user-identifiable strings in logs; store only salted fingerprints
Consider later extension to cross-model namespace for identical shared system prompts
Early experiments show ~18% hit-rate on repeatable system prompt templates in internal traces
